answer: Each identity binds one registered island survey licence, issued only after a survey voyage to that island: it records tide-gauge readings for 30 days and files them with the registry, which checks gauge serial and AIS track. One licence backs one identity; duplicates are rejected. Per fake this costs 1,900 units — 1,500 charter plus a 400-unit fee — and 30 days. One hundred fakes cost 190,000 units, 3,000 days and 100 voyages. The cheapest cheat is buying another's licence, but the seller surrenders the licence backing their own identity; forged tide logs fail serial and track cross-check.
